title: Streetscapes: Large-scale Consistent Street View Generation Using Autoregressive Video Diffusion
control_family: layout, box, map or BEV conditioning

output_modality.value: single-view street-view image sequences along a camera path, generated two frames at a time (512x512) and extended autoregressively; optional 3D reconstruction

control_signal.value: overhead street map plus height map rendered into per-view G-buffers (semantics, disparity, height) for a given camera trajectory; optional text for city style, weather, time of day

control_mechanism.value: G-buffer-conditioned ControlNet cloned with motion modules, base diffusion U-Net kept frozen so text control is inherited; autoregressive temporal imputation at inference

base_model.value: pretrained text-to-image latent diffusion model with an AnimateDiff-style motion module for two-frame generation; ControlNet added

datasets.value: Google Street View posed imagery with map data; pairs of 512x512 images within 80 s and 5 m; London maps for InfiniCity comparison; test maps from unseen regions

metrics.value: LPIPS over the first 16 views for short-range accuracy; FID and KID for long-range realism

controllability_evidence.value: Mostly qualitative: outputs follow the layout and camera poses over 100 frames covering 160 to 176 m; text changes weather and time with the same G-buffers. Table 2 numbers are not in the packet.

closed_loop.value: No: no driving policy; autoregressive rollout along a user-given camera path, 100 frames over more than 170 m shown.

stated_limitations.value: Transient objects such as cars sometimes appear or vanish unnaturally; slight frame-to-frame colour flicker from the quality-consistency balance.

notes: A city-scale street-view generator, not an ego-vehicle driving world model; control is by map layout, camera pose and text rather than ego actions.
